question: Where is Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology, a unit of the Department of Atomic Energy situated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Raja Ramanna Centre for Advanced Technology (RRCAT) is located in **Indore, Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• RRCAT was established in 1984 by the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) of the Government of India.
 
• The center is named after Dr. Raja Ramanna, a renowned Indian physicist and a key figure in India's nuclear program.
 
• RRCAT focuses on research and development in the areas of particle accelerators and lasers, contributing significantly to India's scientific and technological advancements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)**

 
 
• The Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) was established in 1954 and is under the direct charge of the Prime Minister of India.
 
• It is responsible for nuclear technology, nuclear power, and nuclear research in India.
 
• DAE oversees various institutions like the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), and Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR).
 
 
 
• **Particle Accelerators**
 
 
• Particle accelerators are devices that use electromagnetic fields to propel charged particles to high speeds and to contain them in well-defined beams.
 
• They are essential tools in physics research, particularly in the study of subatomic particles.
 
• Applications of particle accelerators include medical treatments (such as cancer radiotherapy), industrial processes, and fundamental scientific research.
 
 
 
• **Lasers**
 
 
• LASER stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation.
 
• Lasers are devices that emit light through a process of optical amplification based on the stimulated emission of electromagnetic radiation.
 
• They have a wide range of applications, including in medicine (e.g., laser surgery), communications, manufacturing (e.g., cutting and welding), and scientific research.
 
 
 
• **Dr. Raja Ramanna**
 
 
• Dr. Raja Ramanna was an Indian physicist who played a crucial role in India's nuclear program.
 
• He is renowned for his work in nuclear physics and was instrumental in the development of India's first nuclear bomb, which was tested in 1974.
 
• He held several prominent positions, including the Director of Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) and the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission of India.
